Rate limiting, quotas, and burst behavior
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-18 16:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Head of ML, Harbor), Ethan Walker (Platform Eng, Harbor), Sofia Alvarez (Security, Harbor)

Summary: casual but focused discovery. Priya leads on model requirements, Ethan asks infra questions, Sofia focuses on compliance. AE/SE describe Redwood integration paths, SDKs, and network options.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, this is Omar on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Singh: Good, thanks. We wanted to do a quick run through of how you'd plug Redwood into our stack, especially around latency and data controls for payments fraud.
[00:18] Omar Ruiz: Awesome. High-level, we support three modes — hosted API for fastest time to value, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private with a customer-controlled control plane (VPC or on-prem). Which of those are you leaning to?
[00:30] Ethan Walker: We're exploring both hosted and dedicated. Hosted is simpler but our security team (Sofia) is picky about PII and residency. For production fraud scoring we need predictable latency and audit logs.
[00:40] Sofia Alvarez: Yeah, key ask: can you do Private/VPC with customer KMS and comprehensive audit logs? And, do you provide RBAC and SSO?
[00:50] Maya Chen: Yes, Private supports customer-managed networking and KMS integration; RBAC and SAML/SSO are supported, and we have audit logs retention options — I'll share the security whitepaper after.
[01:05] Priya Singh: Great. On the integration side, we use LangChain and some in-house LlamaIndex wrappers for retrieval augmented generation. Do you have first-class adapters?
[01:18] Omar Ruiz: We do. We provide official SDKs in Python and JS, plus connector examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. We also have sample repos showing streaming responses, function calling, and how to wire in retrievers. The LangChain adapter supports async streaming and token-level callbacks.
[01:35] Priya Singh: Important for us is KV cache behavior — when we do RAG with long contexts, we want to avoid re-encoding prefixes on every request. How does caching and batching work?
[01:48] Omar Ruiz: Our serving runtime supports prefix KV caching and continuous batching. For RAG flows where you hit the same context a lot, KV cache avoids re-computation for repeated prefixes; batching is workload-aware so we avoid latency spikes. There are configuration knobs per deployment type.
[02:05] Ethan Walker: On our infra, requests flow through an API gateway that does auth and rate-limits; we then call downstream. Will Redwood be fine behind our gateway/proxy? Any special headers or TLS requirements?
[02:18] Maya Chen: Totally standard. For hosted we accept HTTPS with bearer tokens; you can pass through correlation headers for tracing. For Private, the control plane sits in your VPC and you can route traffic internally. We also support mTLS for dedicated/private when required.
[02:35] Sofia Alvarez: And for quotas & rate limits — we need predictable throttling policies. Can we map our gateway limits to Redwood rate limits or quota windows?
[02:46] Omar Ruiz: Yes, Redwood has per-key quotas and per-route rate limits. You can configure burst sizes and smoothing windows. We also expose quota usage in the console and via API so your gateway can pull consumption metrics to enforce upstream decisions.
[02:59] Priya Singh: How about concurrency for batching? If we have many small requests from event-driven functions, we don't want token wait time to go huge.
[03:12] Omar Ruiz: You can set per-route latency SLOs which will change batching aggressiveness. For low-latency paths we disable long batching and prefer smaller, faster batches. For throughput heavy offline jobs you can favor max throughput.
[03:28] Ethan Walker: For the POC, we'd probably route a small sample of production traffic through dedicated capacity to measure p95 latency versus our current model. What's the usual on-boarding timeline for that?
[03:40] Maya Chen: For Dedicated it's typically 2-4 weeks to provision and a couple of days to validate pipelines. For Private (VPC) add time for networking setup and KMS integration — usually 3-6 weeks.
[03:53] Sofia Alvarez: Audit logs — we need immutable logs stored for 12 months and exports to our SIEM. Is that possible?
[04:04] Maya Chen: Yes, we have long retention add-ons and log streaming to S3/Cloud Storage or direct SIEM integrations. We also support event hooks for trace exports.
[04:16] Priya Singh: Omar, can you go over the SDK example for LangChain? We mostly use Python async chains and want to understand token callbacks and tool/function support.
[04:28] Omar Ruiz: Sure — our Python SDK has a LangChain wrapper that implements the LLM interface. It supports stream callbacks (on_new_token, on_done), function/tool calling, and structured outputs via JSON schema. For LlamaIndex we have an adapter that maps index.query to the Redwood SDK with optional embedding caching. I can share a repo with a sample notebook.
[04:49] Priya Singh: Perfect. For the notebook, include an example of using a local retriever with your streaming responses so we can measure end-to-end latency.
[05:00] Omar Ruiz: Will do. Also we'll include an example for using the SDK behind a proxy with custom auth headers.
[05:09] Ethan Walker: About cost — we need an estimate for token unit costs and the economics of quantized model variants. Do you offer recommendations for quantization per workload?
[05:21] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend model and quantization profiles based on your workload. For embeddings vs generation vs chat, different quantization levels make sense. We'll provide example TCO sheets comparing hosted CPX vs Dedicated reserved capacity numbers.
[05:36] Sofia Alvarez: If we run a private deployment, who holds the keys for telemetry? We need the ability to disable telemetry to Redwood HQ.
[05:45] Maya Chen: In Private deployments, telemetry can be configured to stay inside your VPC; by default we ship anonymized metrics, but you can opt to disable any external telemetry — that's a supported enterprise setting.
[05:58] Priya Singh: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex and embeddings? We generate embeddings in-house and want to control embedding keys and rotation.
[06:09] Omar Ruiz: You can push precomputed embeddings to the Redwood embedding index or host embeddings entirely on your side and only use our LLMs; our adapters accept external embedding providers. For key rotation, our API keys can be rotated via the console and we support per-route API credentials.
[06:24] Ethan Walker: For observability, we need tracing at the token and request level and correlation with our logs. What hooks do you provide?
[06:33] Omar Ruiz: We emit request-level traces with OpenTelemetry-compatible spans, per-token hooks for streaming, and a trace id you can pass in request headers so Redwood traces map to your logs. Token-level cost breakdowns are available in the console and via API.
[06:50] Priya Singh: That helps. On model fallbacks and routing — if Dedicated runs out of capacity can I automatically fallback to hosted variant?
[07:00] Maya Chen: Yes, Smart Routing supports fallbacks by policy. You can configure prioritized routes — Dedicated first, then hosted cheaper tier, then a smaller model variant. Fail open or fail closed is configurable per-route.
[07:14] Sofia Alvarez: For compliance, we also do periodic external audits — can Redwood provide architecture diagrams and evidence for SOC2 controls?
[07:24] Maya Chen: Absolutely, I'll share the SOC2 report and the architecture diagrams. For Private we provide an extra bundle of artifacts for audits.
[07:33] Priya Singh: Let's talk about a pilot. We want to run 10k QPS sampled traffic for fraud scoring tests — what's the best approach?
[07:44] Omar Ruiz: For high QPS you probably want Dedicated with reserved capacity sized to your expected p95 CPU/GPU usage. Also use our caching layer for repeated contexts and warm up KV cache. We'll help size batching parameters to meet your latency SLOs.
[07:59] Ethan Walker: Do you support autoscaling within Dedicated? We have spiky traffic.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options. The policies allow min/max capacity and cool-down windows.
[08:13] Priya Singh: A practical question — we use Hashicorp Vault for secrets. Can we integrate KMS with that or do you require cloud KMS?
[08:24] Omar Ruiz: We integrate with cloud KMS providers natively, and for Private you can bring your own HSM/KMS; Vault can be used to rotate API keys and store credentials — we have examples in the integration doc.
[08:37] Sofia Alvarez: Network topology: if we do Private, does the control plane talk to Redwood HQ? We need to ensure no customer PII leaves our VPC.
[08:47] Maya Chen: The Private control plane can be fully customer-hosted; by default no PII is sent to Redwood HQ. We only send aggregated anonymized telemetry (optional). We'll include network diagrams.
[08:59] Priya Singh: Questions from my side are done. Ethan, do you have anything else on infra?
[09:05] Ethan Walker: One more: do you have SDK rate-limit retry patterns or client-side throttling examples? We do not want to hammer the endpoint.
[09:15] Omar Ruiz: Yes, SDKs include retry/backoff strategies and client-side throttling helpers. We'll share code snippets for token bucket style local throttling and exponential backoff with jitter.
[09:27] Maya Chen: Quick recap — we'll send: 1) hosted vs dedicated TCO sheet, 2) security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts, 3) LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo + notebook demonstrating streaming and retriever flow, 4) network diagram for Private, 5) suggested autoscaling and quota configs.
[09:46] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Timeline-wise we want a scoping call next week and then a pilot in ~2 weeks if the numbers look reasonable.
[09:56] Maya Chen: Perfect. Omar, you'll lead the technical scoping?
[10:00] Omar Ruiz: Yep, I'll run the scoping with Priya and Ethan — schedule it for next Tue/Wed.
[10:06] Sofia Alvarez: And I'll review the security docs with you offline.
[10:10] Priya Singh: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:12] - End of recording -

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (Redwood product names sometimes mis-typed as 'Redwood Infer' or 'Red wood'). Natural speech present, interruptions minimal.
